lead.t: Infection cues: Inquire about fever, cough with hemoptysis or night sweats (tuberculosis), dysuria, skin breaks, or animal contacts (leptospirosis).

snip.t: Infection cues: Inquire about fever, cough with hemoptysis or night sweats (tuberculosis), dysuria, skin breaks, or animal contacts (leptospirosis).

Pallor and jaundice: Scleral icterus with pallor indicates brisk intravascular or extravascular hemolysis (severe falciparum malaria, sickle cell hyperhemolytic or aplastic crisis, sepsis-induced DIC, or leptospirosis).
| Leptospirosis | Conjunctival suffusion, calf pain, jaundice | Occupational water exposure, renal failure common |
Leptospirosis: Can cause AKI through direct tubular damage and interstitial nephritis.
Infectious: HIV‑associated nephropathy, disseminated TB, severe malaria, leptospirosis
Infections: legionella, leptospirosis, streptococcal orgs, TB, hantavirus, EBV, E coli (10-15% of cases)
Clinically confused with other causes of febrile jaundice: malaria, viral hepatitis A, B and E, leptospirosis, and other viral haemorrhagic fevers such as dengue, Lassa and Ebola
